sec: Pathophysiology: three pillars and ominous octet

items.q: The page's older-discoveries diagram begins with how many pillars?
items.exp: The heading immediately above the liver, pancreas and skeletal-muscle diagram is 3 pillars. (Book p918)

items.q: Match the three pillar to the printed abnormality — 1) Liver 2) Pancreas 3) Skeletal muscle … A) Increased gluconeogenesis with increased glucose output B) Defective insulin secretion from beta cells C) Impaired receptor function and insulin-dependent glucose-uptake impairment
items.exp: The page maps liver to increased gluconeogenesis and glucose output, pancreas to defective beta-cell insulin secretion, and skeletal muscle to impaired receptor function and glucose uptake. (Book p918)

items.q: The skeletal-muscle pillar names insulin-dependent glucose uptake through ___.
items.exp: The skeletal-muscle column explicitly names GLUT-4 in insulin-dependent glucose uptake. (Book p918)

items.q: Assess the three-pillar notes: I The liver line calls increased gluconeogenesis the most important factor. II The skeletal-muscle line describes insulin resistance.
items.exp: The liver column marks increased gluconeogenesis as the most important factor, while the skeletal-muscle column ends in insulin resistance. (Book p918)

items.q: What does the page give for the ominous octet's count?
items.exp: The ominous-octet heading states that it involves previous 5 and 5 new factors. (Book p918)

items.q: Match the ominous-octet label to the note below it — 1) G 2) P 3) R 4) A … A) Incretin effect B) Pancreas with increased glucagon production C) Renal activation of SGLT-2 D) Adipose tissue with centripetal obesity
items.exp: The octet row gives G for gut/incretin effect, P for pancreas/increased glucagon, R for renal SGLT-2 activation, and A for adipose tissue/centripetal obesity. (Book p918)

items.q: The renal branch in the printed flowchart shows increased SGLT-2 activation followed by increased absorption of:
items.exp: The renal branch shows increased SGLT-2 activation, increased glucose, sodium and water absorption, and oedema. (Book p918)

items.q: Which target is named by the page for the renal component of the ominous octet?
items.exp: The renal arm of the printed octet specifically identifies increased SGLT-2 activation. (Book p918)

items.q: Assess the adipose-tissue flowchart: I Centripetal obesity converts alpha-3 receptors to beta-3 receptors. II The beta-3 receptor line increases lipolysis by hormone-sensitive lipase.
items.exp: The adipose-tissue diagram shows centripetal obesity, conversion to beta-3 receptor activity, and increased lipolysis by hormone-sensitive lipase. (Book p918)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among the four tissues explicitly listed in the skeletal-muscle note for GLUT-4?
items.exp: The GLUT-4 box lists skeletal muscle, heart and adipose tissue; liver is not in that box. (Book p918)

items.q: After increased free fatty acids reach the liver through the portal system, the highlighted main substrate for increased gluconeogenesis is:
items.exp: The flowchart labels FFA as the main substrate leading to increased gluconeogenesis in the liver. (Book p918)

items.q: The bottom note states that insulin also plays a role in T2DM by acting on ___.
items.exp: The final note on the page reads that insulin acts on HSL and plays a role in T2DM too. (Book p918)

items.q: In the page's adipose-to-liver sequence, increased lipolysis produces increased ___ that travels through the portal system.
items.exp: The printed sequence runs through increased FFA via the portal system to the liver. (Book p918)
